diagnostic_evidence.quote: maximizing the value of the \emph{target function} measuring the least deviation of the given subspace from all the same-dimensional coordinate subspaces. Doing this for a large number of samples, we accumulated a set of the resulting subspaces corresponding to the greatest target function value. In all the experiments we have conducted for various $n$ and $k$, this value was equal to $\arccos(1 / \sqrt{n})$.

issues.failure_explanation: The target function Distance(A) measures the least deviation (largest principal angle) of subspace A from the coordinate subspaces, and for an extremal subspace converges to arccos(1 / sqrt(n)). Because arccos(1 / sqrt(n)) > 1 / sqrt(n) for all n >= 2 (for instance, at n = 2, arccos(1 / sqrt(2)) = pi/4 ~ 0.7854 whereas 1 / sqrt(2) ~ 0.7071), comparing d directly against 1 / sqrt(n) + epsilon causes the condition on line 8 of Algorithm 2 to evaluate to true on any extremal subspace. Consequently, the algorithm prematurely prints that the hypothesis is disproven and returns -1, rather than reaching line 11 to record the subspace in ES.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In lines 8 and 11 of Algorithm 2, replace '1 / sqrt(n)' with 'arccos(1 / sqrt(n))' (or 'acos(1 / sqrt(n))').
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 2 fails its contract; it aborts and returns -1 instead of collecting and returning the set of extremal subspaces ES.
issues.title: Incorrect threshold in extremal subspace calculation algorithm
issues.why_classification: A direct, local correction of the threshold in Algorithm 2 restores the algorithm's intended operation and guarantees without affecting any theoretical results or proof architecture in the paper.
